responsibilities: Analyze inventory trends and generate reports to drive decision-making and support supply chain optimization.
Monitor and maintain optimal inventory levels across the supply chain network, balancing service levels with working capital targets.
Collaborate with demand planners and buyers to align inventory strategies with sales forecasts and promotional plans.
Lead root cause analysis for inventory discrepancies, stockouts, overstock, and slow-moving items.
Identify and implement process improvements related to inventory planning, replenishment, and warehouse efficiency.
Develop KPIs and dashboards to track inventory accuracy, turns, cycle times, and other performance metrics.
Support inventory reconciliation and cycle count programs in coordination with warehouse and finance teams.
Assist with ERP system optimization, particularly related to inventory modules, safety stock parameters, and reorder points.
Provide insights into inventory risk and obsolescence to support product lifecycle management.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Speed language ("move fast", "hyper-growth", "a little chaos") roughly balances the trust and reconciliation language ("trusted models, metrics", "inventory reconciliation").
evidence.domain_risk: balancing service levels with working capital targets
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Supply-chain inventory analytics affects operational and working-capital decisions without regulatory or financial-reporting framing, so it is moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: data engineering; finance; product; operations; demand planners; buyers
evidence.data_team_maturity: you'll build and evolve our enterprise semantic layer
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An enterprise semantic layer and data engineering function exist and are still evolving, so it is mid-stage.
evidence.jd_authorship: Support inventory reconciliation and cycle count programs in coordination with warehouse and finance teams.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The prose names a precise stack (dbt, Airflow, Spark, StarRocks, Omni), but the bullets read like a generic inventory-analyst template.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll partner closely with data engineering, finance, product, and operations
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Supply-chain operations, finance and leadership are served with no single dominant audience.
evidence.autonomy_level: This is a high-ownership role for someone who wants to shape how the company understands its data and how decisions get made.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns analytics for the supply-chain team and leads root-cause analysis.
evidence.ai_role: to deliver everything from executive dashboards and AI analyst agents to well-defined, reusable data models
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate delivers AI analyst agents on top of the semantic layer, so AI sits downstream of their work.
evidence.testing_framing: strong software engineering practices (testing, CI/CD, code review)
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing appears only in the preferred qualifications, without an ownership verb in the responsibilities.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Lead root cause analysis for inventory discrepancies, stockouts, overstock, and slow-moving items.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Discrepancies and inventory risk are operational concerns secondary to analysis and reporting.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: build and evolve our enterprise semantic layer
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Building and evolving an existing semantic layer is a mixed mission.
evidence.loss_aversion: Lead root cause analysis for inventory discrepancies — an operational concern.
